prompt:
Draw exactly ONE new Small Seal font glyph from the attached reference image. It shows FOUR historical specimen slots of the SAME character labelled THX, CCZ, QJZ and DYC; any slot marked UNAVAILABLE is absent evidence. Study ALL AVAILABLE specimens equally. Reconstruct one coherent attested whole form with the original ancient identity; do not combine incompatible variant components, imitate only THX, or substitute a modern Chinese character.

Build genuine smooth stroke trajectories as original harmonious Gothic monoline drawing, with absolutely CONSTANT stroke width around 3% of the full canvas. All strokes must share that width, with round caps and round joins, smooth rounded curves and precise straight bars, no taper, swelling, brush outlines, serifs, pressure modulation, textures or blobs. Keep every required counter and gap clearly open. Essential bar length relationships, branches, descending legs, tiny detached marks and contacts are structural requirements, not decoration.

Use a square 1:1 canvas. Center the ONE glyph inside the central70% with generous clear margins. Output ONLY pure BLACK constant-width strokes on a fully TRANSPARENT background, with no labels, text, codepoint, chart, grid, background, frame, shadows, watermark or multiple specimens. Exactly one complete glyph.

Explicit structural/proportion reading aid:
U+3D076. THX, CCZ and QJZ are AVAILABLE; DYC is unavailable, do not invent its evidence. LEFT component: vertical stem with THREE horizontal bars, bottom only modestly longest; top80–95% bottom, middle comparable or shorter. RIGHT UPPER cluster has THREE distinct long courses: (1) LEFT upright/bracket turns inward RIGHT at its bottom and carries TWO short inward rightward ticks above that return; (2) CENTER gently S-curving upright stem with ONE short arm projecting RIGHT near top and ONE short arm projecting LEFT around middle; (3) RIGHT upright/bracket turns inward LEFT at bottom and carries TWO short inward leftward ticks above that return. Keep both side brackets separate from central S with clear gaps. Central S starts a little taller than side brackets. No enclosed upper counters invented. BELOW, with a clear gap in coherent THX form, TWO mirror-like inward-opening curled hand forms, left and right. EACH hand has an outer C-like rounded course opening toward center, with TWO free inward-directed ends (upper and lower), plus ONE short inward diagonal/curve branching into outer side near middle; total THREE inward terminals per hand. From each outer hand-side junction one LONG vertical leg descends to baseline: exactly TWO long lower legs total. Keep center between hands OPEN, never join their inward ends into counters. Preserve all top bracket ticks, central S arms, both three-terminal curled hands and both lower legs.

visual_review.method: white inspection composite compared against all available reference specimens
reading_criteria: Only THX/CCZ/QJZ available; do not infer DYC.
Three upper courses: two brackets each with two inward ticks plus basal return, central S with top-right and middle-left arms.
Two lower curled hands each have three inward free terminals and one long descending leg; no counter or bridge between hands.
Left three-bar stem bottom only modestly longest.
notes: Three available witnesses and enlarged forms compared. Native retains all upper ticks/S arms and mirrored lower three-terminal hands with exactly two long legs.
No invented closed counters; lower central space open.
caveats: Narrow gaps separate upper bracket returns/central S from lower hand tips; tracker and heavier weights must preserve these detachments.
QJZ can detach the central left mark; chosen THX/CCZ-style arm remains joined to S.
